# Jack Macdonald | Macdonald Group of Compass

> Jack Macdonald is a Bellevue native and REALTOR with Macdonald Group of Compass, helping people buy and sell homes across Bellevue, Redmond, Kirkland, Issaquah, Sammamish, Woodinville, Bothell, Kenmore, Newcastle, Renton, North Bend, Fall City, Carnation and Shoreline on the Eastside of Seattle, Washington. This site publishes monthly market reports, area guides, neighborhood guides, school district guides, city comparisons, and buyer and seller guides written from years of local experience.

Contact: 425.941.6998, 700 110th Ave NE, Suite 270, Bellevue, WA 98004. Washington license 21022645.

## Market reports (updated monthly)

* [Bellevue Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/bellevue/index.md): Bellevue single family homes sold at a median price of $1.72 million over the August through October 2026 period, down 2.9% from $1.77 million the same stretch last year. Fewer homes traded hands too, 253 sales compared to 314 a year ago, a drop of 19.4%. Supply has grown to 3.0 months and the median time on market has stretched to 27 days, up from 8 days a year ago.
* [Redmond Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/redmond/index.md): Redmond single family homes sold at a median price of $1.52 million over the August to October 2026 period, down 10.3% from $1.70 million in the same 3 month window last year. Volume fell too, with 91 homes sold compared to 113 a year ago. Supply has grown to 3.0 months and the median days on market stretched to 28 days, up from 20 last year.
* [Kirkland Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/kirkland/index.md): Kirkland single family home sales over the August to October 2026 period show a median sale price of $1.27 million, down 19.3% from the same 3 month window last year when the median was $1.57 million. Volume picked up, with 252 homes sold compared to 227 a year ago. Homes are sitting longer too, a median of 27 days on market versus 13 days last year, and supply has grown to 2.9 months from 2.0 months.
* [Issaquah Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/issaquah/index.md): Issaquah single family homes sold at a median price of $1.62 million over the August through October 2026 window, up 8.8% from the same stretch last year when the median was $1.49 million. Fifty four homes sold, a modest dip from 58 the year before, and the typical home found a buyer in 14 days. Supply has loosened a bit, with months of supply now at 3.1 compared to 2.0 a year ago.
* [Sammamish Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/sammamish/index.md): Sammamish single family home sales from August through October 2026 show a median sale price of $1.48 million, down 10.2% from the same 3 month window last year when the median was $1.65 million. 155 homes sold over the period, compared to 173 a year ago. Supply has grown notably, with months of supply at 2.9 versus 1.3 last year, and homes are sitting about a month before selling.
* [Woodinville Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/woodinville/index.md): Woodinville single family homes sold at a median price of $1.27 million from August through October 2026, up 2.4% from the same 3 month window last year. Only 20 homes sold compared to 28 a year ago, and supply rose to 3.9 months from 2.6. With a market this size, any one month can move the numbers around, so take these figures as a snapshot rather than a firm direction.
* [Bothell Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/bothell/index.md): Bothell single family home sales from August through October 2026 show a median sale price of $1.13 million, essentially flat from $1.14 million over the same 3 month stretch last year. Eighty one homes sold, nearly identical to the 82 sold a year ago, and homes averaged 33 days on market compared to 29 days last year. The bigger shift is in supply: months of supply has grown from 2.1 to 4.5, giving buyers noticeably more room than they had twelve months ago.
* [Kenmore Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/kenmore/index.md): Kenmore single family homes sold at a median price of $1.09 million over the August to October 2026 period, down from $1.17 million during the same 3 month window last year. Forty three homes changed hands, compared to 59 a year ago, and supply has grown to 3.6 months from 2.3 months. Homes are still moving in a median of 20 days, and sellers are getting 98.2% of their list price on average.
* [Newcastle Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/newcastle/index.md): Newcastle single family home sales ran 27 transactions over the August through October 2026 period, down from 54 in the same 3 month window last year. The median sale price came in at $1.55 million, about 2.7% below the $1.59 million recorded a year ago. Homes averaged 35 days on market, and months of supply has grown to 3.1, up from 1.6 last year.
* [Renton Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/renton/index.md): Over the August to October 2026 period, 160 single family homes sold in Renton at a median price of $716,000, down 5.2% from $755,000 during the same 3 month window last year. Homes are sitting on the market longer too, with the median days on market at 34 compared to 17 a year ago. Supply has grown to 2.8 months, up from 1.8 months last year, and the number of sales dropped 12.1%.
* [North Bend Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/north-bend/index.md): In North Bend, the median sale price for single family homes was $1.20 million over the August to October 2026 window, down from $1.32 million in the same 3 month period last year. 36 homes sold, the same count as a year ago, and homes spent a median of 22 days on market compared to 30 days last year. With only 36 sales in this window, the numbers can swing a lot from month to month, so take any single figure as a snapshot rather than a firm direction.
* [Fall City Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/fall-city/index.md): Six single family homes sold in Fall City over the August to October 2026 window, with a median sale price of $924,000 and a median of 63 days on market. That median price is down 10.0% from the same 3 month window last year, when the median was $1.03 million across just 4 sales. With only 6 homes in the sample, any one sale can move these numbers considerably, so treat them as a snapshot rather than a firm signal.
* [Carnation Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/carnation/index.md): Carnation saw 17 single family homes sell over the August through October 2026 window, with a median sale price of $1.09 million, down from $1.20 million in the same 3 month window last year. Homes averaged 32 days on market and sold at 98.7% of list price, with 2.3 months of supply available. That said, with a small pool of sales like this, one or two outlier transactions can move the numbers considerably, so take any year over year comparison with some caution.
* [Shoreline Home Values & Market Report | Updated November 2026](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/market-reports/shoreline/index.md): Over the August through October 2026 window, 84 single family homes sold in Shoreline at a median price of $805,000, down 8.1% from $875,000 during the same stretch last year. Homes are sitting on the market a little longer too, with a median of 14 days compared to 17 a year ago, and supply has grown from 1.7 months to 3.6 months. Fewer homes are changing hands overall, with sales volume down 22.2% from the 108 that sold in the same 3 month window last year.

## Area guides

* [Bellevue area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/bellevue/): Bellevue is the Eastside's largest city, from the high rises downtown to established neighborhoods like Somerset, Newport Hills and Bridle Trails. I grew up here, so this is the market I know street by street.
* [Redmond area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/redmond/): Redmond runs from a fast growing, walkable downtown out to Education Hill, Overlake and Redmond Ridge. Light rail, Microsoft and the Lake Washington School District shape a lot of what buyers ask about here.
* [Kirkland area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/kirkland/): Kirkland pairs a lakefront downtown with very different neighborhoods a few minutes away, from Houghton and Rose Hill to Juanita and Finn Hill. It is one of the most requested areas on the Eastside for buyers who want to be near the water.
* [Issaquah area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/issaquah/): Issaquah sits at the edge of the Cascade foothills along I 90, with a historic downtown, the Issaquah Highlands, and hillside neighborhoods on Squak and Cougar Mountain. Trails start practically in town.
* [Sammamish area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/sammamish/): Sammamish is a plateau of mostly single family neighborhoods between Lake Sammamish and the foothills, served by both the Lake Washington and Issaquah school districts. Lots tend to be larger than in the closer in cities.
* [Woodinville area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/woodinville/): Woodinville sits in the Sammamish River valley north of Redmond, known for its wineries, the Sammamish River Trail, and neighborhoods spread across the hills on both sides of the valley. Much of the city is in the Northshore School District.
* [Bothell area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/bothell/): Bothell straddles the King and Snohomish county line along I 405, with a rebuilt downtown on the Sammamish River, the UW Bothell campus, and established neighborhoods like Canyon Park and North Creek. Most of it is in the Northshore School District.
* [Kenmore area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/kenmore/): Kenmore sits at the north end of Lake Washington where the Sammamish River meets the lake, with the Burke Gilman Trail running through town and quick access to Bothell and Kirkland. It is in the Northshore School District.
* [Newcastle area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/newcastle/): Newcastle is a small city between Bellevue and Renton on the slopes of Cougar Mountain, with trail access into Cougar Mountain Regional Wildland Park, a golf course with views of Lake Washington, and quick access to I 405.
* [Renton area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/renton/): Renton sits at the south end of Lake Washington, with Gene Coulon Park on the lakefront, The Landing, and neighborhoods from Kennydale and the Highlands to Talbot Hill. I 405 and SR 167 meet here, which makes it an easy base for commuting north or south.
* [North Bend area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/north-bend/): North Bend is a small mountain town at the base of Mount Si, about 30 minutes east of Bellevue on I 90. Buyers come for space, acreage and the outdoors, and the trade off is the drive.
* [Fall City area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/fall-city/): Fall City is an unincorporated river community along the Snoqualmie River between Issaquah, Snoqualmie and Carnation. Homes here are often on larger rural lots, and the market is small, so every sale moves the numbers.
* [Carnation area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/carnation/): Carnation is a small farm town in the Snoqualmie Valley, where the Tolt River meets the Snoqualmie, between Duvall and Fall City. Homes here are often on larger rural lots, and the market is small, so every sale moves the numbers.
* [Shoreline area guide](https://jackmacdonaldre.com/areas/shoreline/): Shoreline sits just north of Seattle between I 5 and Puget Sound, with Richmond Beach on the water, light rail stations at 148th and 185th, and established neighborhoods of mostly single family homes. It is served by the Shoreline School District.
